source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

source_merge_reasons.13:1: The inherited public 13:1 combines source Rev 12:18 with Rev 13:1. Both source payloads retain their exact separate hashes; public labels and the 404-verse layout are preserved.

next_scope: Draft complete through Revelation 22; independent review, queued whole-book reviews, reader testing and Companion reconciliation remain pending
completed_block_scope: 2 Peter 2–3; 1 John 1–5; 2 John 1; 3 John 1; Jude 1; Revelation 1–22

notes: “Revelation of Jesus Christ” and “testimony of Jesus” can indicate what comes from Jesus or what concerns him.
Asia here names the Roman province in western Asia Minor. “Seven spirits” is retained without replacing the number with an interpretation.
The pinned Greek reads “freed”; another reading is “washed.”
“One like a son of man” echoes the humanlike figure of Daniel 7:13.
The word translated angels can also mean messengers; their precise identity is not supplied.
vocabulary: A bright or refined copper alloy, conventionally burnished bronze; the exact metal is uncertain.
Hades, the realm of the dead.

notes: The charge concerns the particular opponents described in this address to Smyrna; the sentence does not name Jews generally as its subject.
“Faith in me” can also be rendered “my faith” or “faithfulness to me.”
The pinned text has “the woman Jezebel”; another reading has “your wife Jezebel.”
The text says “bed,” without an explicit sickbed term. “Kill with death” may suggest death by plague. Children may denote descendants or adherents.
Kidneys and hearts are bodily images for the inner life.
The iron-rod language echoes Psalm 2:9. The pinned verse 28 begins “just as I too have received from my Father.”
vocabulary: Kidneys, used with hearts for inward thought and feeling.

notes: The accusation repeats the localized opponent description in 2:9.
“Keep you from” does not specify whether protection occurs through the testing or by removal from it. “My word of endurance” can refer to the call to endure or the endurance associated with Jesus.
“Beginning” can indicate origin or source as well as the first in a sequence.
The Greek verb means vomit; the bodily image is retained.
The pinned edition places a sentence break before the last “after these things” in verse 1, linking it with verse 2. Other punctuation attaches it to “what must happen.”
The spatial expression says “in the midst of the throne and around the throne”; it is not replaced with a reconstructed arrangement.
The pinned text reads “they existed and were created”; other witnesses vary the wording and order.
The Lamb stands while appearing slaughtered; both parts of the image remain.
The pinned text does not say “bought us.” Verse 10 reads “them,” “kingdom,” and the present “they reign.” Other witnesses vary the pronouns and use a future reign.
vocabulary: Slaughter; the same violent verb describes human victims elsewhere in the vision.

notes: The pinned summons is simply “Come”; some witnesses add “and see.”
“Death” can also denote pestilence in the list of sword, famine, death and beasts.
The Greek says that the fellow slaves should be “completed”; the rendering supplies their full number. The expression can also be understood in terms of their course being completed.
The pinned text reads “their wrath”; another reading has “his wrath.”
vocabulary: A dry measure of roughly a liter, often a person’s daily grain ration.
Denarius, a Roman silver coin; elsewhere a day’s wage for a laborer.

notes: The list includes both Joseph and Manasseh, and does not name Dan or Ephraim. The names are not harmonized with other tribal lists.
The Greek uses a present participle: “those coming out.” Washing robes white in blood is left as an image.
vocabulary: Pitch a tent or dwell; here spread a tent over.

notes: The text says a third of the earth, a third of the trees, but all the green grass; the quantities are not harmonized.
The pinned text reads “eagle”; another reading has “angel.”
The pinned text mentions the altar’s horns without the added “four” found in some witnesses.
The Greek number is twice ten thousand times ten thousand: two hundred million.
vocabulary: The Hebrew name evokes destruction; the Greek name means destroyer.
Potions or magical preparations, here sorceries; not a general designation for medicine.

notes: The Greek says “time will no longer be”; in this sequence it can mean that there will be no further delay.
The Greek uses a completed form for the fulfillment set in the seventh angel’s days.
The source has the plural “they say”; no speakers are identified here. “About” may also carry the sense “over” or “against.”
The object of “I will give” is not expressed; authority is supplied from the context.
The Greek alternates a collective singular “body” with plural “bodies.” The English uses bodies for the two witnesses. “Spiritually called” introduces the names Sodom and Egypt.
The pinned text reads “they heard”; another reading has “I heard.”
The pinned acclamation has “who is and who was,” without the “who is coming” used earlier.
The source says both “son” and “male,” and uses the shepherding verb with the iron rod.
“A time, times and half a time” is retained rather than converted to a single unit.
The pinned source has a separate verse 18, “He stood on the sand of the sea.” The inherited public layout places it at the start of 13:1; both original records are separately bound there.
vocabulary: Royal crown or diadem, distinguished from the wreath-crown term elsewhere.

notes: The opening sentence follows source 12:18, which reads “he stood”; another reading has “I stood.” The remainder is source 13:1. Public numbering remains unchanged.
The pinned text places “those who dwell in heaven” after “his dwelling” without another and.
“From the foundation of the world” can modify the writing of names or the slaughtering of the Lamb. The Greek places it at the end; compare 17:8.
The pinned wording concerns going into captivity and being killed by the sword. Other readings speak of taking captives or killing and then receiving the same fate.
“A human number” may also mean “the number of a man.” The pinned text reads 666; some witnesses read 616. No individual is named here.
vocabulary: An engraved, impressed or branded mark.

notes: The pinned text includes “like” before “a new song.”
The text describes male virgins not defiled with women. Readings differ over literal celibacy and symbolic fidelity; the image is not replaced with either interpretation.
The word rendered passion can also mean fury or wrath, giving the wine image a further possible resonance.
“Faith of Jesus” may indicate faith in Jesus or Jesus’ faithfulness.
“From now on” may attach to dying in the Lord or to the ensuing rest.
vocabulary: A distance of roughly 185 meters; 1,600 stadia is roughly 300 kilometers or 185 miles.

notes: The preposition can mean standing on or beside the sea of glass. “Harps of God” can indicate their divine source.
The pinned text reads “King of the ages”; other witnesses read “nations” or “saints.”
The pinned reading is linen; another reading has stone.
vocabulary: Tent of testimony, the sanctuary expression retained in the vision.

notes: The pinned text reads “the holy one,” not the later “who shall be” wording.
The text makes the altar the speaker.
The first-person announcement interrupts the vision; no new speaker is named in the verse.
The Greek gathering verb is singular after the preceding plural spirits; it can treat the neuter plural collectively, or leave a singular agent implicit.
vocabulary: Harmagedon, also conventionally Armageddon; its precise derivation is debated.
Weighing about a talent, an ancient heavy weight of roughly 30–40 kilograms; exact standards varied.

notes: “Mystery” can describe the name or be understood as part of the inscription.
The pinned text ends “will be present”; other witnesses vary the last part of the temporal formula.
The seven mountains are also seven kings. The text gives the five/one/other and eighth/from-seven relationships without naming the kings.
The pinned text reads “the ten horns ... and the beast”; another reading relates the horns as being on the beast.
vocabulary: Prostitute; used here in the city’s personification.

notes: The pinned text includes the final clause about unclean and hated beasts; some witnesses omit it.
The pinned reading is “have fallen”; another widespread reading is “have drunk.”
The Greek ends the cargo list with “bodies, and human souls/lives,” language that exposes human beings traded as slaves.
The pinned final verb is third-person plural, “they will not find,” amid the direct address to the city.
The compressed judgment phrase may mean that God has judged their case against the city or imposed on her the judgment she inflicted on them.
vocabulary: An aromatic spice; its precise botanical identity is uncertain.

notes: The pinned text has the future “we will give”; other readings continue the exhortation “let us give.”
“Testimony of Jesus” can mean testimony from Jesus or testimony about him. The relation to “spirit of prophecy” is not expanded into a definition.
The pinned text reads “dipped in blood”; another reading has “sprinkled with blood.” The source of the blood is not named.
vocabulary: A Hebrew expression meaning praise the LORD.

notes: The syntax connects the beheaded witnesses with those who refused the beast; it does not explicitly settle whether two distinct groups are intended. “Came to life” and the thousand years are retained without an added chronological system.
Gog and Magog are named in the vision; they are not replaced with later geographical identifications.
Death and Hades remain distinct from the lake of fire into which they are thrown.
vocabulary: Execute by beheading, associated with an axe.

notes: The pinned text reads the plural “peoples”; other witnesses have the singular “people.” Its final clause ends “God himself will be with them.”
The pinned completed verb is plural, rendered “these things are done.”
“My son” retains the scriptural sonship formula in a promise addressed to the one who overcomes.
The verse gives the wall’s measurement without specifying height or thickness.
Ancient gemstone names do not always match modern mineral classifications. The conventional names retain the twelvefold sequence.
The pinned text has “the nations,” without the expansion “of those who are saved.”
vocabulary: Stadion and cubit: ancient length units. 12,000 stadia is roughly 2,200 kilometers; 144 cubits roughly 65 meters.

notes: The syntax permits different attachments of “in the middle of the street” and “on either side of the river.” The tree of life is singular while described on both sides.
The throne is of God and of the Lamb, followed by singular his and him; these pronouns are not replaced with explanatory names.
The pinned text reads “God of the spirits of the prophets”; other witnesses vary this expression.
The pinned text reads “wash their robes”; another reading has “do his commandments.”
The pinned text reads “tree of life”; some later texts have “book of life.”
The pinned ending is “with all.” Other witnesses expand the recipients or add Amen; no final Amen is added here.
vocabulary: Freely, as a gift, without payment.
